clue.text: Some of those Vera loved — quite a number

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wistful remark that Vera had a good many lovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Several means more than two but not many, i.e. a fair handful or quite a number.

clue.text: No longer having little room, hospital department is first-class

parts.note: ex- means former, no longer so
a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A patient complains of losing their tiny room, yet praises the hospital department as superb.
explanation.definitionFit: Excellent and first-class are synonyms for outstanding quality.

clue.text: Officials, people telling others to 'old their tongue?

definitions.meaning: court or church attendants who show people to seats are officials

definitions.text: people telling others to 'old their tongue
definitions.meaning: a court usher calls for silence; dropping the H, Cockney style, as in ''old', also turns hushers into the answer

explanation.surface: A wry look at officials whose job seems to be telling people to keep quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''old' (hold with its H dropped) hints that the answer is HUSHERS with the H dropped too.
explanation.definitionFit: Ushers are officials in courts and ceremonies, and in court they call for silence.

clue.text: Sections of American agents in groups

indicators.note: the agents are placed in the groups, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: sets are groups of things
G-men are FBI agents in American slang

explanation.surface: Talk of divisions within US agencies whose agents work in teams.
explanation.definitionFit: Segments are parts or divisions of a whole, the same as sections.

clue.text: Moving feebly, tourist at famous sight in America

indicators.note: moving shifts the letters of the next three words into a new order

explanation.surface: A weary tourist shuffles along at a well-known American landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' rearranges the letters of FEEBLY TOURIST AT.
explanation.definitionFit: The New York harbour statue is one of the best-known landmarks in the United States.

clue.text: Heartless man is thug, horrible person with weapons

indicators.note: horrible suggests a messed-up state, so these letters are scrambled
taking the heart out of a word leaves only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted thug who is a nasty piece of work, and armed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' leaves MN of MAN; with IS and THUG, 'horrible' rearranges MNISTHUG.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunsmith makes and repairs firearms, so works with weapons.

clue.text: Make law — stick up document finally

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: An order to legislate, or else post the paperwork on a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns CANE into ENAC in this down clue; 'finally' adds T from document.
explanation.definitionFit: To enact a bill is to pass it into legislation, making it a law.

clue.text: Irish politician going about unaccompanied is somehow able to grasp things

indicators.note: the politician goes around the other word, enclosing it

parts.note: TD stands for Teachta Dála, a member of the Irish parliament
alone means with no one else

explanation.surface: An Irish politician touring on their own somehow manages to understand things.
explanation.definitionFit: A taloned creature has claws, so it is equipped to grip and seize things.

clue.text: Gender king switched over — one of the ancient kings

indicators.note: switched over says the two words together are turned around end to end

parts.note: sex is a synonym for gender
rex is Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch's gender swapped, set beside the rulers of antiquity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switched over' turns SEXREX round, end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: Xerxes was a Persian ruler of the fifth century BC.

clue.text: Woman of the upper classes, friend when Christmas comes round

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name
U denotes upper-class usage in British English
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A posh lady and her chum turn up when Christmas does.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done annually happens once a year, as often as each Christmas arrives.

clue.text: Like hot desert home that's most calm

parts.note: sere means dry and parched, as a hot desert is
a nest is a home, for a bird or figuratively

explanation.surface: A sun-baked desert dwelling described as the most peaceful place.
explanation.definitionFit: Serene means tranquil, so its superlative is the most tranquil, or most calm.

clue.text: In this there will be praying mantis on the move

definitions.text: In this there will be praying

indicators.note: on the move suggests the letters shifting into another order

explanation.surface: A praying mantis scuttles about, so the insect is literally praying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'praying mantis' is a famous insect, misleading from the morning service; 'on the move' rearranges MANTIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Matins is the morning service of prayer in the church.

clue.text: Man perhaps following car having left city

indicators.note: following says this piece comes after the ones before it

parts.note: the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland, is one example of an island

explanation.surface: A man left behind as a car drives away from town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, a self-governing island in the Irish Sea, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Carlisle is a cathedral city in Cumbria, north-west England.

clue.text: Unfashionable parts of city away from the centre

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
wards are electoral districts of a city

explanation.surface: The dowdy districts of a town lie on its edges.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving outwards means heading toward the edge, further from the middle.

clue.text: Everybody I have upset scoffed, revealing temper

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: upset tips the contraction over, so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: I've is the contraction of I have
to scoff is to eat greedily, so scoffed gives ate

explanation.surface: Someone flustered that the whole lot has been gobbled up, and shows their bad mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns IVE into EVI. 'temper' is the verb, to moderate or soften, not anger.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper is to moderate or soften, just as relieving lessens a hardship.

clue.text: One carving out a living?

parts.note: carving out a living normally means earning one with effort, but the person here literally carves for a living, in stone or wood

explanation.surface: Someone making their way in the world by hard graft.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist who shapes stone or wood into figures earns their bread by chiselling.

clue.text: Professional army officer keeping to correct procedure

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside

parts.note: pro is short for professional
Col is the abbreviation for colonel

explanation.surface: A career soldier of rank sticking to the rule book.
explanation.definitionFit: Protocol is the established code of proper conduct and etiquette.

clue.text: It's not original material, article about tailless insects

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: lice are small parasitic insects
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An observation that some fabric is a copy, with an aside about bugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' here just means concerning; the article is set after the cut-down insects. REP is a ribbed fabric used for upholstery and ties.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is a copy, so by nature it is not the original article.

clue.text: Loud way of talking putting daughter off stories

parts.note: f, for forte, is the musical mark for loud

indicators.note: putting something off means removing it

parts.note: diction is a manner of speaking
d is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A loud manner of speech puts a daughter off listening to tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiction is invented narrative, i.e. made-up tales and novels.

clue.text: There may be pollutant gases here? It's uncertain

definitions.text: There may be pollutant gases here?
definitions.meaning: literally, gases hang in the atmosphere
the idiom for something undecided or still pending

explanation.surface: A puzzle over where the fumes are, and doubt about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans that are up in the air are undecided, and fumes float aloft literally.

clue.text: Leaders in public health in city once getting prize

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: Troy is the ancient city of Homer's Iliad

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Pioneers of public health in a historic city winning an award.
explanation.definitionFit: A trophy is a cup or award given to a winner.

clue.text: Seem to change sides finally, making request for money?

indicators.note: the last letter swaps one side for the other, right becoming left

parts.note: appear means seem

explanation.surface: A politician seeming to defect at the last, and then asking for funds.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) is the final letter of APPEAR; changing sides makes it L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: A charity appeal is a plea for donations, a request for cash.

clue.text: Poet in small room, endlessly upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the letters bottom to top
endlessly drops the final letter

parts.note: the smallest room is a euphemism for the lavatory

explanation.surface: A poet sitting in a tiny room, eternally troubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts TOILET to TOILE; 'upset' turns that round to give T. S. Eliot's name.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot wrote The Waste Land and is a major modern poet.

clue.text: Selfish types, say, to sit around and start to swank

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as 'say' does

indicators.note: around suggests the letters being moved about
start to takes the first letter

explanation.surface: Vain people lounge about and begin to show off.
explanation.definitionFit: Egotists are conceited people preoccupied with themselves.

clue.text: Menacing coming from the left

definitions.meaning: in heraldry and Latin, ... means on the left-hand side

explanation.surface: Something threatening approaching from the left.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means threatening, and in its Latin origin and heraldry means left-sided.

clue.text: Old cricketer building three-figure score

parts.note: a hut is a small building
a ton is a hundred, a cricket century

explanation.surface: A veteran batsman notching up a century.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Len Hutton was a celebrated England opening batsman of the 1930s to 1950s.

clue.text: Festival flower, one left out in the wind

parts.note: Easter is the Christian spring festival

indicators.note: out means left out, removed from the word

parts.note: a lily is a flower
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An Easter lily missing from the decorations, blown about in a breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes I and L from LILY, leaving LY. Easter lilies are white spring flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: An easterly is a wind blowing from the east.
